$GOOG - I bought more of this the second earnings came out. Moved 2% which just seemed way too low for 63% cloud growth. Earnings kind of doesn't matter right now, everyone is doing accelerated depreciation on their CAPEX. People bicker about how long GPUs are monetizable (is it 3 years or 7?!) - for starters, its probably at least 5 years, good starting point. But secondly, 40% of the CAPEX is stuff that lasts way longer than that, like buildings and power generation. That stuff is getting fully depreciated in one year, and then lasts for 30!

If they keep up 63% cloud growth while having Search continue to maintain 19% growth, $GOOG is def in the pole position for ASI.

$VEON reported overnight, great numbers. Market cap is 3.44b.
- Rev increased 17% YoY. EBITDA up 17.7% to 517m. Equity free cash flow 246m - these are quarterly numbers, so, 3.4x FCF or under 1.5x EBITDA.

- Digital revenues grew 57.7% YoY to USD 303 million, representing 25.2% of Group revenue; digital EBITDA was USD 105 million (34.6% margin)
- Financial services revenues grew 41.0% YoY to USD 135 million - Jazz is probably the best digital (maybe best overall?) business in Pakistan.

VEON is an amazing company, but a terrible stock, with Ukraine war overhang and Pakistan macro looking brutal. That said, the Kazakstan macro is much better, and the numbers are good enough that I think eventually everything just gets worked out and you end up with a very strong diversified cash generating machine. I am very long this one, though not a recommendation.

text:
We’re in the middle of a technological Cambrian explosion and the effects of every tiny bottleneck immediately going limit up the second some autist discovers it might actually be underestimated.

Like, ‘what’s next, glass substrates? Ok let’s just 10x all those companies and let them do another ATM’.

This is always how manias drive innovation (read about the British bicycle bubble of the 1890s for an interesting analog), but it feels like this might just be the new normal - if you are a Swiss watch maker that pivots to actuators for humanoid robots, someone WILL find you and then, within some VERY broad guidelines, you’re basically granted unlimited capital. The turnaround time feels extremely fast, and the breadth is every technological market at this point, from Israeli drone cameras to Swedish Lazer designers, Japanese glass substrate manufacturers, 3rd tier Taiwanese chip designers…

It feels much more like VC investing but rather than the long targeted VC process it is just the entire market allocating. Investment research tools have gotten very good, the AI helps a lot with quickly nailing harder science, social media is extremely powerful…. All feels pretty bullish.

Co-sign, have followed them for a while now (initially $EXAS/ $NTRA, now long $PSNL and $CAI. Looking into $WGS here too though haven’t got that spot down cold like the others).

It’s also worth following $TEM if you are into this space though I do not think it is a long personally, it is always too expensive and the business is quite hard to understand (unlike PSNL/NTRA where they just sell u a test that tells u if ur cancer is coming back and u take it as often as your possibly allowed to since it saves ur life - there, now you understand those two businesses too).

Currently think $CAI is best after the big $PSNL run up but not selling that one any time soon either.

Cancer diagnostics is a great business and also really obvious to me that it will massively benefit from AI (already is). The frontier labs always roll out “curing cancer” to justify their value, well, this is how that works, these are the companies using diagnostics data to determine treatment, track reoccurrence, determine effectiveness of the immunology, etc.

I will write a post on these this coming month I think, find it super interesting and unlike event driven bio, u can just fill in your little spreadsheet each quarter with the new volume numbers, like tending to your garden. 🪴
